terra.problem: The text does not say nobody asked for treasure or that the nations showed up with nothing to eat or drink. It says they did not meet Israel with food and water.
The claim that nobody hired Achan to curse anybody goes beyond what the cited texts say.
The passage names Balaam as the man hired, but it does not say Korah was never hired by Ammon or Moab.
Saying the people who hired Balaam walked away with a blessing for the other side adds an outcome for them that the passage does not describe.
The refund punchline makes the LORD turning the curse into a blessing the subject of the joke.
The verse gives the LORD's love as the reason; it does not say it was not because of anything Israel did or said.
The comparison suggests that the tenth generation of Ammonites and Moabites may enter. Verse 3 says they may not enter even to the tenth generation.
Contrasting the tenth generation for Ammon and Moab with the third generation allowed to enter suggests that the tenth may enter. Verse 3 says the opposite.
The referee joke compares the LORD to someone Papa would pay to settle arguments, making God the subject of the joke.
The passage does not say the man had no say before taking refuge.
This is a flat restatement of the answer and verse, with no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The explanation simply rejects the word, quotes the verse, and repeats the answer. It sounds generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
The verse forbids putting grapes in a basket; it does not state a general prohibition on taking any grapes home.
The verse forbids putting a sickle to the grain, not merely bringing one. It also does not limit the hand-plucked grain to a few heads.
The passage does not give the sickle's use as a harvesting tool as the reason for the prohibition.
